correctness.rationale: For a>0 the kernel h(s)=s^(−p)exp(−a/s−ks) vanishes at 0, and the sign of a−ps−ks² gives a unique mode m≤a/p. The release-phase derivative is proportional to h(t)>0. After release the derivative is proportional to h(T+δ)−h(δ); it is positive when both arguments lie before m and negative when both lie after m. On the intermediate interval the first term strictly decreases and the second strictly increases; endpoint signs give a unique crossing and global peak with δ<m<T+δ. The logarithmic equality at the peak gives a/δ−a/(T+δ)=p log(1+T/δ)+kT. For z=a/(pδ)>1 and B=log(pT/a)+kT/p, its exact rearrangement is z−log z=B+E, with 0<E≤2a/(pT). The large branch has z>B; evaluating x−log x at x=B+log B underestimates B by log(1+log B/B). For B≥2, the derivative is at least 1/2 throughout the comparison interval, so 0<z−(B+log B)≤2 log B/B+4a/(pT), uniform even for arbitrarily large k(T). This proves the displayed lag and all three scaling regimes. The derivative at the crossing also gives the stated strict duration trends. The supplied finite-grid script and metadata were inspected, not executed; uniformity follows from the analytic inequality, not the grid.
